fields.statement: At e4375da1 (attempt 2, review cycle 2): go test -count=1 ./internal/api -run TestAddQuestionLenientRefs passes (a run session's question 'Use @@store, not @@ghost?' is written, stored as @@{<full ID>} for store and literal @@ghost, shown as 'Use @@store, not @@@@ghost?'). go test -count=1 ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/(text-refs-write|text-refs-engine-writes|run-ship-change-rebase|describe-golden) passes: text-refs-write.txtar now writes a 20-char ID prefix and greps the full ID stored, and shows a note's @@nowhere as @@@@nowhere; text-refs-engine-writes.txtar shows question answer's Decision as 'Use @@other, not @@@@ghost' with the quote verbatim; run-ship-change-rebase.txtar conflicts on a file named @@shipping, stores the question statement with @@{<ID>}, and re-raising writes nothing (log bytes cmp equal). Mutation check in a scratch worktree: dropping the resolved-statement comparison in ship_rebase.go makes run-ship-change-rebase.txtar fail at line 203, so the dedupe test is sensitive. Scratch-build probe (clean env): rhiza add capability bad --field statement=@@nosuch exits 4 naming '@@nosuch in field statement' with next 'fix the handle, or write @@@@ for a literal @@', also with --dry-run, and writes nothing. guide text internal/guide/text/rhiza.md:82 tells agents to write @@handle. make check: fmt-check, vet and test pass; self-check fails only on text-ref-check-verified (evidence for leaf text-ref-check, commit efb07bd4, not this leaf) holding a literal @@{01ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ}.
